stem: (Select TWO.) Meridian Robotics looks at every infrastructure update in a pull request before merging it into the shared branch. Which two practices does Terraform's team workflow recommend around plan review?

choices.text: Treat an approved pull request's plan as accurate no matter how long ago it was generated
Review the plan's proposed actions during the pull request so teammates can catch mistakes before anything is merged
Have the reviewer read only the configuration diff in the pull request, without looking at the plan's proposed actions
Immediately before applying the merged branch, generate and review the plan again to account for any change to the branch or state file after the pull request was reviewed
Have each engineer apply their own changes from their own laptop instead of through the shared, reviewed branch workflow

rationale: Reviewing plan output in the pull request, and reviewing a fresh plan again right before the merged apply, are both part of the recommended team workflow. Treating an old plan as still accurate ignores that the branch or state can move after review. Reading only the configuration diff misses the concrete add, change and destroy actions the plan proposes, which is the thing the review is meant to catch. Applying independently from individual laptops bypasses the shared, reviewed process.
